jobs.title: Infrastructure & Platform Operations Engineer
jobs.excerpt: ABOUT DYSRUPITDysrupIT is a consulting-led technology firm.
jobs.description:
ABOUT DYSRUPIT

DysrupIT is a consulting-led technology firm. We help mid-market to enterprise businesses solve business problems through technology — whether that's consulting, execution, managed services, or staff augmentation — and we take accountability for the outcome. We are dedicated to making a positive impact in the communities we serve.

COMPANY CULTURE

At DysrupIT, success isn't measured in headcount placed or hours billed — it's measured in outcomes delivered. We're a team that takes ownership of the work, stays curious about problems beyond our immediate scope, and builds relationships meant to grow, not just renew or end. We invest in our people with the training and support they need to grow their careers, and we back a culture where everyone, regardless of role, is encouraged to notice opportunities, ask one more question, and help lead the story for our clients, not just deliver it.

JOB SUMMARY

The Infrastructure & Platform Operations Engineer supports, maintains and improves the infrastructure and production platforms used to deliver Nephos services to customers. The jobholder works across cloud / on-premise infrastructure, Linux, networking, databases, containers, monitoring and enterprise platforms, with a strong initial focus on BAU production support, service stability and knowledge transfer. As capability develops, the role will also contribute to platform change, upgrades, automation and project delivery.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Working hours: 9–5 UK hours during onboarding and transition, with flexibility for occasional out-of-hours upgrades, changes and major incidents.

  • Work as part of Service Operations to support enterprise infrastructure and production platforms, including health monitoring, issue resolution, proactive maintenance, resilience and continuous improvement.
  • Administer, support and troubleshoot customer environments, including core infrastructure, storage, networking, IAM awareness, compute resources and managed services relevant to supported platforms.
  • Support Linux environments, primarily Ubuntu and Red Hat, using command-line administration and troubleshooting techniques; provide appropriate support for Windows where required.
  • Diagnose complex network and connectivity issues across TCP/IP, DNS, routing, firewalls, VPNs, TLS, proxies, load balancers and cloud networking.
  • Administer and support PostgreSQL production environments, including configuration, roles and permissions, monitoring, backup and restore, recovery, performance investigation and upgrades.
  • Administer and support MongoDB production environments, including health, logs, performance, backup and recovery, upgrades and troubleshooting.
  • Support containerised and orchestrated environments using Docker and Kubernetes, including container lifecycle, logs, configuration, volumes, networking, registries, health checks, resource constraints and failure diagnosis.
  • Support cloud container services and clusters, including AWS with EKS and ECS where applicable, and contribute to platform configuration, health and capacity management.
  • Monitor infrastructure and applications using enterprise monitoring and observability tools, including alert investigation, log analysis, threshold review, root-cause identification and reduction of unnecessary alert noise.
  • Use scripting and automation, particularly Python and PowerShell, to improve repeatability, reduce manual effort and support operational tasks; Bash or other transferable scripting experience is also valuable.
  • Use Git and GitHub to manage scripts, configuration and operational content, following appropriate version-control practices.
  • Support enterprise platform installations, configuration, upgrades, testing, validation and recovery, including data platforms such as BigID and internally developed solutions such as Nephos-developed platforms where customer access is approved.
  • Learn and develop operational capability in new or unfamiliar enterprise platforms quickly, using structured knowledge transfer, documentation, practical shadowing and independent task completion.
  • Take ownership of Incident and Problem records, applying structured troubleshooting to identify issues, restore service as quickly and safely as possible, complete root-cause analysis and maintain accurate records.
  • Take ownership of Service Requests and technical operational tasks, ensuring work is completed accurately, securely and within agreed priorities.
  • Manage Change records relating to infrastructure, databases, platforms, upgrades and improvement activity, attending CAB where required and ensuring implementation, validation and rollback plans are appropriate.
  • Create and maintain clear knowledge articles, runbooks and work instructions, and actively participate in cross-training so that critical operational knowledge is not concentrated with one individual.
  • Work directly with customer and internal technical teams during incidents, changes, upgrades and investigations, explaining findings clearly and maintaining a professional, customer-focused approach.
  • Collaborate with DevOps, Data Services, Product, Delivery and other cross-functional teams to resolve issues and deliver end-to-end platform outcomes.
  • Contribute technical input to platform improvements, resilience, capacity, monitoring and operational design. Final architecture and governance decisions remain shared internal responsibilities.
  • Support backup, restore and disaster-recovery activities, including practical validation and recovery exercises.
  • Work in accordance with security principles including least privilege, secure credential handling, secrets, certificates, auditability, patching and vulnerability awareness.
  • Access to individual customer environments remains subject to the relevant customer contractual, security and access approval processes.
  • The role is focused on operating, supporting, deploying and improving production platforms rather than developing application functionality.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Typically 5+ years of experience in infrastructure engineering, platform operations, systems engineering or production support; demonstrable capability is more important than a fixed number of years.
  • Strong, practical BAU and production support experience, including ownership of live incidents, service restoration, monitoring, failed changes or deployments, root-cause analysis and controlled remediation.
  • Strong hands-on AWS experience in production environments. AWS is the primary cloud requirement for this role.
  • Very strong demonstrable Linux administration and troubleshooting experience, particularly Ubuntu and Red Hat, including confident command-line use.
  • Deep practical networking and connectivity troubleshooting experience covering TCP/IP, DNS, routing, firewalls, VPNs, TLS and cloud networking.
  • Strong production MongoDB administration and troubleshooting experience. This is a critical capability for the role.
  • Meaningful PostgreSQL operational experience, including administration, backup and recovery, monitoring and troubleshooting; deeper production DBA experience is highly valued.
  • Hands-on production experience with Docker and a strong working knowledge of container lifecycle, networking, logging, health and troubleshooting.
  • Strong hands-on Kubernetes experience, including deployment health, pods, services, configuration, logs and failure diagnosis.
  • Experience supporting enterprise applications and platforms through installation, configuration, version upgrades, health monitoring and technical troubleshooting.
  • Strong scripting and automation capability, particularly Python and/or PowerShell; experience with Bash or other transferable scripting languages is also relevant.
  • Strong monitoring and observability fundamentals, including infrastructure metrics, log investigation, alert analysis and distinguishing symptoms from root cause.
  • Excellent issue analysis, troubleshooting and fault-finding skills, with a methodical approach to complex production problems.
  • Working knowledge of Git and GitHub, including repositories, version control and collaborative working practices.
  • Practical understanding of backup, restore, recovery and service-resilience principles.
  • Practical IT service management experience covering Incident, Problem, Change, Service Request and major-incident processes. Formal ITIL certification is not mandatory.
  • Experience using a service-management platform such as Jira/JSM, ServiceNow, Remedy, Freshservice or equivalent.
  • Good security awareness, including least privilege, IAM concepts, secrets, certificates, MFA, privileged access, patching, vulnerability awareness and secure credential handling.
  • Strong customer-centric attitude with the ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders during normal operations and incidents.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear technical documentation and operational procedures.
  • Demonstrable ability to learn complex unfamiliar technology and become independently effective following structured onboarding and knowledge transfer.
  • Able to work independently following onboarding, manage multiple priorities and recognise when escalation or wider technical input is required.
  • Flexible, organised and self-motivated, with willingness to participate in occasional out-of-hours upgrades, changes and major incidents where required.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Hands-on Azure experience. Azure is expected to become increasingly relevant, although AWS remains the primary current requirement.
  • Experience with Google Cloud Platform and services such as Cloud Run or Cloud SQL.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code principles and tooling such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD platforms and deployment pipelines such as GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI or Azure DevOps.
  • Previous experience with BigID or another complex enterprise data-governance platform. BigID experience is not required, but the ability to learn it is important.
  • Experience with RabbitMQ, Redis or similar messaging/cache technologies.
  • Experience with LogicMonitor or comparable enterprise monitoring platforms.
  • Experience using privileged-access and secrets-management technologies such as Delinea and HashiCorp tooling.
  • Experience with REST APIs and API troubleshooting.
  • Experience in applying, renewing and troubleshooting TLS certificates.
  • Experience with disaster-recovery planning, RPO/RTO considerations and practical recovery testing.
  • Knowledge of data governance, information security or regulated customer environments.
  • Relevant AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, MongoDB or ITIL certifications. Certifications are advantageous but not mandatory.
  • Experience supporting microservices, serverless or distributed platform architectures.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Competitive compensation package commensurate with experience.
  • Government-mandated benefits plus supplemental HMO coverage.
  • Collaborative and professional work environment.
  • Career growth opportunities within a growing technology organization.
  • Hybrid/Remote work arrangement (where applicable).

BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description:

  • The Analytical Technical Lead (ATL) is the single global point of contact and accountable owner for analytical lifecycle management of assigned commercial products across major markets (US, EU, China, Australia, Canada) and supports Rest of World (RoW) expansion and post-approval maintenance.

  • At Director level, this role is responsible for making risk-based, inspection-defensible decisions on methods, specifications, stability, and analytical investigations across a distributed internal/external QC network for small molecule products.

  • This leader ensures the analytical control strategy remains robust over the product lifecycle, drives harmonization, and enables reliable supply while meeting GMP, pharmacopeial, and regulatory expectations.

  • The Analytical Technical Lead (ATL) may own relevant global business processes, ensure compliance and efficiency.

Essential Functions of the Job:

A. Global Analytical Point of Contact (PoC) for Approved Commercial Products

  • Act as the global PoC for all analytical-related matters for assigned products, to ensure analytical readiness.

  • Provide governance and technical leadership for analytical topics spanning drug substance (DS), drug product (DP), and critical raw materials/reagents as applicable.

  • Translate global product strategy into aligned expectations and deliverables for internal QC sites, external QC labs/CMOs, AST, and MST.

B. Analytical Lifecycle Management: Changes, Deviations, and Investigations

  • Lead and approve strategy for analytical investigations and performance issues (OOS/OOT/OOE, atypical results, invalidations), ensuring scientifically sound root cause analysis and effective CAPA, including method optimization.

  • Drive analytical change control impact assessments and execution plans, including method updates, revalidation/verification, reference standard changes, and instrument/software upgrades.

  • Own escalation management for supply-critical analytical events; align actions with Quality, Regulatory, and Supply Chain.

C. Global Business Process & Knowledge Owner: Methods, Specifications, Stability, Retest/Shelf Life

  • Serve as global business process and knowledge owner for:

    • Commercial analytical method lifecycle (validation/verification strategy, transfers, periodic review, trending, method robustness improvements)

    • Global specifications governance (release and stability), including harmonization and lifecycle updates

    • Stability program ownership (protocol strategy, commitments, pull schedules, trending, annual review narratives)

    • Retest period/shelf-life governance (extensions, commitments, labeling impacts, country-specific constraints)

  • Take over “submission-ready” documentation sources from development: analytical control strategy, method history, validation packages, specification rationale, and stability trend narratives.

  • Ensure defensible alignment between analytical control strategy and product risk profile (CQAs/CPPs), including small-molecule impurity control.

D. Regulatory Support: RoW Filings and Post-Approval Variations

  • Provide analytical SME leadership for global regulatory submissions relevant to QC:

    • RoW filings (Module 3 analytical sections, stability commitments, method/spec alignment)

    • Post-approval changes (variations, supplements), including comparability narratives and analytical bridging

  • Partner with Regulatory CMC on health authority interactions and responses related to analytical controls, stability trends, and specification justification.

E. Partner and Network Oversight (Internal QC and External Labs/CMOs)

  • Provide governance for external QC networks: align expectations, metrics, investigation quality, and issue escalation pathways (with ESQ as needed).

  • Contribute to audits/inspections as product analytical SME; ensure inspection readiness for assigned products and analytical systems.

  • Influence lab capacity planning and capability upgrades with a risk-based view.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • N/A

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of Biopharmaceutical with significant commercial lifecycle responsibility experience required

  • Master’s degree and 7+ years of Biopharmaceutical with significant commercial lifecycle responsibility experience preferred

  • Doctoral Degree and 5+ years of Biopharmaceutical with significant commercial lifecycle responsibility experience desired

Computer Skills:

  • Strong PC literacy required; MS Office skills (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Other Qualifications:

Experience

  • Demonstrated leadership in GMP QC and/or analytical sciences for:

    • Small molecule methods (HPLC/UPLC, GC, dissolution, residual solvents, elemental impurities, genotox impurities as applicable)

  • Strong working knowledge of method validation/verification, stability trends and statistical evaluation, specification lifecycle management, and data integrity.

Leadership Competencies

  • Ability to lead through influence in a matrix organization; strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills.

  • Strong technical writing and ability to deliver inspection-defensible narratives.

  • Program and risk management mindset; ability to prioritize in supply-constrained environments.

Travel: Up to 20%

Global Competencies

When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.

jobs.excerpt: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations.
jobs.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.



About the Role:

CrowdStrike's Data Science team mis seeking a Sr. Manager to lead a team of data scientists at the intersection of Machine Learning, Large Language Models, and Cybersecurity/reverse engineering. This is a leadership role where you will help the team manager business demand/needs, translate them to technical objectives, gain stakeholder buy in, and help drive the technical approaches and provide technical feedback and guidance to junior and experienced team members.

As a technical leader you will support you team in identifying high-value problems in the short, mid, and long term, obtain stakeholder buy in, and translate problems in the business into actionable research objectives. You'll collaborate and work with all aspects of ML and cybersecurity, across a large enterprise and complex data problems in size (trillions of events a day), asperity, and the dynamic nature of an active adversary that adapts to our advances in the field.

This role is a chance to work in impactful outcomes that improve people's security and safety, while also growing in depth and breadth. From assemble, lifting, decompilation to optimal control and continuous optimization, every problem in the spectrum of computer science and related disciplines occurs in tackling the problems CrowdStrike deals with. An excellent candidate will have a intrinsic desire to learn and leverage tools across these domains, invent new tools to fill the gaps in what we need, and a desire to increase their leverage by enabling a team to perform these critical research objectives.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead and mentor a team of data scientists, providing technical guidance, career development, and performance management

  • Work with senior leadership to refine/define priorities, identify risks/gaps, support staff and budget planning, and disseminate key milestones to the business leaders.

  • Plan and prioritize team roadmaps, balancing research innovation with delivery of production ML systems

  • Stay current with emerging trends in ML and cybersecurity, and evaluate new technologies for potential adoption

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including security research, engineering, and product to align ML capabilities with business objectives

  • Partner with security domain experts to identify high-impact opportunities where ML can enhance threat detection and response

  • Communicate complex technical concepts and ML insights to stakeholders across the organization

  • Guide the development of advanced models for malware detection, behavioral threat analysis, and AI-driven security automation

  • Drive research initiatives that result in publications, blog posts, patents, and other contributions to the ML and security communities

  • Contribute to hands-on technical work when needed, maintaining deep expertise in ML systems and security applications

What You’ll Need:

  • Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, or related STEM field, OR Bachelor’s degree with equivalent experience

  • 5+ years of experience in data science and machine learning

  • 5+ years in a technical leadership or team lead capacity

  • Proven track record of leading ML projects from research to production deployment

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders

  • Ability to present and work with senior stakeholders in a business, communicate risks/opportunities, and translate business problems into technical objectives

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, and ability to keep track of multiple projects, and distill key details for regular program management.

  • Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

  • Deep expertise in cybersecurity, including experience in threat intelligence, malware analysis, or security operations

  • Experience with agentic AI systems, LLMs, or autonomous security automation

  • Track record of working with very large, sparse, high-dimensional datasets in production environments

  • Experience with advanced ML techniques including semi-supervised learning, online learning, and model optimization for reducing false positives

  • Strong knowledge of ML operations, including model monitoring, A/B testing, and production ML infrastructure

  • Comfortable working in cloud environments (AWS) and Linux systems

  • Proven ability to set technical vision and drive innovation in ML systems

  • Experience hiring, building, and scaling high-performing data science teams

  • Strategic mindset with ability to balance research exploration with pragmatic business outcomes

Additional Qualifications:

  • Published research, patents, or contributions to the ML or security communities


Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike:

  • Market leader in compensation and equity awards
  • Comprehensive physical and mental wellness programs
  • Competitive vacation and holidays for recharge

Join Apaleo and shape the future of hospitality tech

Apaleo is the world’s most open, API-first property management platform, powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Our modular, AI-powered infrastructure lets hoteliers customise their tech stack, automate routine work and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.

If you’re driven by the idea of making hospitality smarter, more human and powered by cutting-edge technology, we’d love to hear from you.

About the role

You’ll join our Platform team as an individual contributor, working directly with our Platform Lead, who sets Platform’s technical direction. Platform owns infrastructure, developer experience and security foundations for the whole engineering organisation. It’s a small team, so you’ll cover a wide surface area, with no dedicated DevOps or QA function to hand work to.

This is a high-ownership seat. You’ll take on substantial, ambiguous, cross-cutting initiatives, agree the direction with the Platform Lead, then drive them from first analysis through to completion with real autonomy over how you get there.

We don’t run a groomed backlog or sprint planning. We assign a significant topic to someone who owns it end to end. If you thrive with structure handed to you, this isn’t the role. If you love spotting the problem worth solving and driving it yourself, you’ll fit right in.

What you’ll be up to

  • Designing and building scalable, reliable and maintainable backend systems.
  • Spotting and scoping problems and initiatives yourself, not just picking up assigned tickets: weighing impact, priority and timing.
  • Contributing to architectural decisions and design discussions, and bringing other teams along.
  • Driving substantial, cross-cutting initiatives end to end, coordinating with stakeholders across engineering.
  • Building and maintaining internal tools and infrastructure (AWS, Terraform) that help teams deliver faster and more reliably.
  • Owning observability, logging and operational excellence to keep the platform highly available.
  • Sharing knowledge through code reviews, design reviews and pairing, and helping raise technical standards.
  • Spotting where AI and automation can improve how we build and run software.

Some of the challenges waiting for you

You’ll take ownership of one of these as your first initiative, with no other distractions.

  • Solving horizontal write-scaling for our database.
  • Modernising our CI/CD pipeline for faster, more reliable delivery.
  • Migrating our infrastructure-as-code fully from CloudFormation to Terraform.
  • Extracting and reworking common services to get us ready for our next scale level.

What you’ll bring to the team

  • 5+ years of backend development experience, with a track record of owning significant technical work from ambiguity through to completion.
  • Substantial hands-on ownership of infrastructure, reliability or performance, ideally on a platform or infrastructure team rather than a pure product team.
  • Strong engineering fundamentals that transfer across languages and cloud platforms. We care more about how you think than which stack you’ve used.
  • Experience designing and scaling distributed systems in cloud-native environments (AWS preferred; strong Azure fundamentals and genuine enthusiasm for the switch work just as well).
  • Comfort with containerised services and infrastructure-as-code (Docker, Terraform; CloudFormation exposure is relevant given our current stack).
  • Confidence writing your own unit and integration tests, as we don’t have a dedicated QA function.
  • A project you can talk about in depth: the problem, what you did and the impact it had.
  • Fluent English.

Nice to have

  • Direct experience with C# (.NET), PostgreSQL, AWS and ECS or Kubernetes: a great fit, though not a hard requirement if your fundamentals are strong.
  • Experience setting up infrastructure-as-code from scratch and working with it day to day, ideally with Terraform, including migrating or consolidating from other approaches (like CloudFormation).
  • Experience with Kafka or other event-driven and streaming systems (Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ or SQS are good transferable equivalents).
  • Experience owning observability and logging for highly available systems.
  • Hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor AI, ChatGPT, Amazon CodeWhisperer) and a genuine interest in AI-driven engineering improvement.
  • Experience mentoring other engineers, and introducing new technology, like AI tooling, to other teams.

Culture & Growth

  • An International Team: Work alongside colleagues from over 20 nationalities.
  • Growth and Development: 360° feedback reviews, an evolving career framework and an annual learning budget of €1,000+.
  • Autonomy and Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We trust you to make decisions and contribute directly.

  • Team Connection: Regular team dinners, company meetups and offsite events.

jobs.description:
Role Description

As a Senior Client Platform Engineer on CorpFleet Engineering, you will own and improve Dropbox’s Windows endpoint platform. You will bring deep Windows and Intune expertise, make patching and application delivery more reliable, and build automation that reduces recurring work for the team.

This is a hands-on role combining Windows technical ownership with the development of a more code-managed endpoint platform. You will help evaluate and adopt FleetDM, osquery, infrastructure-as-code, and GitOps practices where they improve reliability, visibility, and maintainability. You will strengthen the current environment while building and validating the path forward—not assume that replacing a tool is the answer.

You will work with CorpInfra, IAM, Security, and support teams to make practical technical decisions, lead multi-phase improvements, and clarify ownership. You will also mentor teammates through pairing, code review, and shared operational practices. This is an individual-contributor role, not a people-management position.

Responsibilities

  • Own endpoint reliability and lifecycle management. Improve provisioning, application delivery, updates, security configuration, and troubleshooting across the endpoint environment.
  • Make patching predictable and safe. Strengthen update workflows through testing, controlled rollouts, and remediation.
  • Make fleet health trustworthy and actionable. Improve reporting on device health, patching, and configuration, with clear ownership for resolving issues.
  • Build maintainable automation. Turn recurring work into reliable, tested workflows that other engineers can operate.
  • Advance code-managed endpoint operations. Adopt tools and practices that improve configuration management, validation, and deployment.
  • Lead cross-functional platform improvements. Define practical roadmaps, resolve dependencies, and balance security, reliability, employee experience, and team capacity.
  • Strengthen the team’s capability. Mentor teammates, review code and designs, and document reusable practices that improve coverage across the endpoint team.

Requirements

  • Significant experience engineering and operating Windows endpoint environments, with personal ownership beyond ticket handling or routine console administration.
  • Deep hands-on Intune experience across device lifecycle, configuration and compliance policies, application management, update workflows, and relevant Entra ID dependencies.
  • Strong Windows troubleshooting skills across operating-system behavior, services, logs, networking, certificates, identity, and security controls. Able to distinguish reported management status from actual endpoint health.
  • Recent ownership of Windows and third-party application patching, including staged deployment, user-impact validation, failed-device handling, exceptions, and recovery.
  • Strong practical PowerShell skills and familiarity with at least one additional programming language, such as Python, Go, or C#. Experience building and maintaining production automation or systems integrations.
  • Demonstrated use of version control, code review, automated checks, and controlled deployment for operational changes. Able to explain safe retries, failure handling, secrets management, and configuration drift.
  • Ability to independently define and deliver multi-phase work, prioritize under ambiguity, partner across teams, and mentor other engineers.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including concise technical decisions, incident updates, runbooks, and effective asynchronous collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Production experience with FleetDM on Windows, including agent operations, policies, queries, targeting, API integrations, or configuration managed through GitOps.
  • Practical osquery and SQL experience for endpoint inventory, health, or security use cases, including query validation, performance considerations, and handling stale or missing results.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code or declarative configuration, continuous integration and delivery, and migration or coexistence between endpoint-management platforms.
  • Experience with Automox, Patch My PC, or comparable tools, and with endpoint privilege management, application control, encryption, or other security controls.
  • Experience supporting developer-heavy, distributed environments and contributing reusable automation across Windows, macOS, or Linux.

Durable Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technologycontinue to evolve:

  • Awareness:Understand yourself and others.
  • Judgment:Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.

  • Connection:Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

We are seeking an experienced Hadoop Solutions Developer to design, build, and operate large-scale data processing pipelines and analytics platforms on Hadoop and related big-data ecosystems. In this role you will be responsible for ingesting, transforming, and analyzing massive volumes of structured and unstructured data to support enterprise analytics, machine learning, and reporting workloads.   • Partner with data scientists and analysts to deliver curated, reliable, and well-documented datasets that accelerate their work.

  • Continuously evaluate and adopt new technologies in the big-data and cloud ecosystem (EMR, Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery) where they offer meaningful improvements.
  • Lead performance reviews and architecture audits of existing pipelines, proposing concrete refactoring and optimization initiatives.
  • Document data architectures, schemas, pipeline behaviors, and operational runbooks in a way that makes the platform supportable as the team scales.
  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to the team’s engineering standards and best practices.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Five or more years of professional experience designing and operating big-data pipelines on Hadoop.
  • Strong hands-on expertise with Apache Spark (Scala, Python, or Java) in production environments.
  • Solid experience with Hive, HDFS, Sqoop, HBase, and the broader Hadoop ecosystem.
  • Hands-on experience with streaming data platforms such as Kafka, Spark Streaming, or Flink.
  • Strong SQL skills and experience working with both relational and NoSQL data stores.
  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow or Oozie.
  • Solid understanding of distributed systems concepts, including partitioning, replication, and fault tolerance.
  • Strong scripting skills in Python or Shell.
  • Excellent troubleshooting, debugging, and documentation skills.
Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Kubernetes-based data platforms (Spark-on-K8s, Trino).
  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code in data engineering workflows.

jobs.title: Founding Product Lead
jobs.excerpt: We’re looking for a Founding Product Lead to help define what HyperDev becomes, who we build for, and how we turn an ambitious vision into a product developers love and use.
jobs.description:
We’re looking for a Founding Product Lead to help define what HyperDev becomes, who we build for, and how we turn an ambitious vision into a product developers love and use.

You’ll work directly with our Founder to own product strategy, customer discovery, and the roadmap, partnering closely with engineering and design to bring ideas to life. You’ll connect what developers need with what our technology can deliver and what will build a sustainable business.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll talk to users, map workflows, prototype ideas, write clear product briefs, and work alongside engineers to ship and improve the experience. You should be comfortable moving between a conversation about company direction and the details of why a developer gets stuck in onboarding.

You’ll bring a founder’s sense of ownership: challenging assumptions, making decisions with incomplete information, and taking responsibility for outcomes after launch. You’ll know when to experiment, when to invest in quality, and when to say “not yet” while keeping the team moving.

Above all, you believe AI should amplify human judgment, and you want to shape how that works in a real product.

RESPONSIBILITIES

You’ll set the product direction

  • Work with our Co-Founders to define the product vision, target users, and the problems HyperDev is best placed to solve.
  • Turn that direction into a focused roadmap, balancing customer needs, commercial opportunities, and technical constraints.
  • Make clear prioritisation decisions, explaining what we’re building, why it matters, and what we’re choosing to defer.
  • Stay close to developments in AI and developer tooling, using that understanding to sharpen our positioning and product choices.

You’ll understand developers and validate demand

  • Build direct relationships with developers and early customers through interviews, workflow observation, and regular feedback.
  • Identify where existing tools fall short and which problems are important enough for users to change how they work.
  • Test assumptions through prototypes, experiments, and early releases before committing substantial engineering time.
  • Bring customer evidence into everyday decisions and close the loop with users as the product evolves.

You’ll turn ideas into useful, well-crafted software

  • Own the product journey from discovery and definition through delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Translate problems into clear product briefs, user journeys, and acceptance criteria that give engineering and design room to solve them well.
  • Work alongside the team to prototype experiences, resolve trade-offs, and keep delivery focused.
  • Take responsibility for the details that make developer tools feel intuitive: onboarding, feedback, error recovery, and the path to a first useful result.

You’ll shape how humans and AI work together

  • Define where AI should act independently, where people should review or intervene, and how users retain control of the result.
  • Partner with engineering to evaluate AI-powered workflows for usefulness, reliability, speed, and cost.
  • Make transparency, understandable outputs, and recovery from mistakes part of the core product experience.
  • Treat trust, security, and code ownership as product requirements from the outset.

You’ll measure outcomes and help build the business

  • Define success measures across activation, engagement, retention, and conversion, with a clear view of the value users receive.
  • Establish lightweight analytics and feedback loops so the team can see what is working and what needs to change.
  • Work with our Co-Founders to test pricing, packaging, and routes to market.
  • Help shape launches, positioning, and product demonstrations that communicate HyperDev’s value clearly.
  • Use evidence from real usage to decide what to improve, expand, or stop.

You’ll help build the founding team and culture

  • Establish a practical rhythm for discovery, prioritisation, and delivery that suits a small, fast-moving team.
  • Help hire and develop the product and design capabilities we need as we grow.
  • Build a culture of curiosity, candid feedback, and shared responsibility for customer outcomes.
  • Keep the team connected to the problem we’re solving and the people we’re solving it for.

About Us

At HyperDev, we don’t believe AI replaces developers. We believe it should make them faster, clearer, and more human.

Our platform turns natural language into real, working software while keeping people firmly in the loop. AI generates structure and logic; humans guide intent, judgment, and quality. The result is code that stays understandable, controllable, and owned by the people building it, not a black box you’re afraid to touch.

HyperDev is a spin-out within the HyperionDev ecosystem, backed by a profitable global tech education company. Our founding team includes engineers who have worked on generative AI models at OpenAI and technical leaders behind award-winning software products. We’re building tools for developers who want leverage, not autopilot.

If you care about craft as much as speed, and you want to shape how humans and AI build software together, you’ll feel at home here.

Requirements

Minimum:

  • Experience taking a software product or significant product area from an early idea through launch and iteration.
  • A track record of owning product decisions and delivering measurable customer or business outcomes.
  • Hands-on experience with customer discovery, prioritisation, and close collaboration with engineering and design.
  • Strong technical fluency: you can discuss APIs, integrations, architecture, and engineering trade-offs with developers.
  • Practical experience building or shipping AI-powered products, with an understanding of the capabilities and limitations of LLMs.
  • Strong product judgment and attention to user experience, supported by evidence and an ability to explain your decisions.
  • Comfort using product data and customer feedback to guide experiments and investment.
  • The ability to move work forward independently in an early-stage environment with evolving priorities.


Preferred:

  • Experience as a founder, founding product hire, or product leader at an early-stage technology company.
  • Experience building developer tools, technical SaaS products, or products used by software engineering teams.
  • A background in software engineering, technical product management, or hands-on prototyping.
  • Familiarity with TypeScript, React, Python, LLM APIs, RAG, or agent workflows.
  • Experience finding product-market fit, testing pricing, or building a product-led growth approach.
  • Experience hiring and growing a small product or cross-functional team.
  • Participation in developer communities or open-source projects.

Benefits

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of the founding team of a new AI developer platform backed by an established, profitable parent company.
  • Shape the architecture, product, and culture of a company from day zero.
  • Collaborate with a team that has worked at OpenAI and shipped award-winning products.
  • Access the resources, backing, and reach of the HyperionDev ecosystem while building something new.
  • Work on the cutting edge of AI and developer tooling, with the freedom to experiment and innovate.

If you’re excited to help build a category-defining product from the ground up and want the ownership and impact that comes with being a founding engineer, we’d love to talk.

jobs.description:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

Role Overview

The Staff Application Security Engineer leads application security strategy for Apollo’s Security department and delivers it through hands-on work and technical leadership. This role takes on the hardest AppSec problems across product, platform, and AI-powered features, including problems with no established playbook.

The role shapes the roadmaps of Engineering, Product, and Platform teams so secure patterns become the default, and sets the AppSec standard that helps many teams build securely without relying on any single person.

Key Responsibilities

AppSec strategy, standards, and influence

  • Lead Apollo’s multi-year AppSec strategy and turn it into multi-quarter, cross-team initiatives that move Security department KRs. Report progress, risks, and tradeoffs to Security leadership on a regular cadence.
  • Shape Engineering, Product, Platform, and Data roadmaps so security work is planned in early, and represent AppSec in cross-department decisions.
  • Set the secure design, code review, and risk model standards used across the department and adjacent engineering teams, including expectations for AI-generated and agent-generated code.
  • Mentor senior engineers and security champions, grow the champions program, and help raise the hiring bar, so the AppSec program does not depend on one person’s expertise.

Secure architecture and vulnerability depth

  • Lead security architecture reviews and threat modeling for ambiguous, high-scale, multi-team systems, including AI and agent features, and define the approach where no precedent exists.
  • Design and drive adoption of secure-by-default building blocks, such as shared authorization, safe OAuth and token handling, and SSRF-safe HTTP clients, so whole classes of issues stop appearing.
  • Shape vulnerability management across internal reviews, bug bounty, pentests, and SCA and runtime findings, with a focus on root causes, bug classes, and clear risk-based severity decisions.
  • Stay hands-on for the hardest cases: read code across teams, develop exploits, test bypasses, and lead variant analysis and staged remediation across teams.

Tooling, automation, and AI (AI-native by default)

  • Set the standard for AI-augmented AppSec in the department. Use AI and agents for code review, threat modeling, triage, and remediation, and build automation that teams outside Security adopt, with measured gains in speed, coverage, and signal quality.
  • Define how Apollo secures its AI systems and agent features, including input and output handling, AI-exposed APIs, prompt and response guardrails, tool permissions, and data-exfiltration paths.

What Good Looks Like(drafted from your mission and success sections)

  • Owns AppSec strategy across a multi-year horizon and gets it committed in other teams’ roadmaps.
  • Solves ambiguous, no-playbook problems and defines the approach for others to follow.
  • Makes hard risk calls under ambiguity and aligns technical and non-technical leaders without formal authority.
  • Builds guardrails, standards, and people so AppSec scales beyond any one person.

Required Skills & Experience

  • A track record of leading AppSec strategy that changed how several engineering teams build, with measurable results, typically backed by 10+ years in software engineering or application security.
  • Expert code review, penetration testing, and exploit development skills, with the ability to find design flaws in unfamiliar codebases and land fixes that hold up against bypass attempts.
  • Strong software development skills and the ability to ship production code. Ruby and Ruby on Rails experience is highly valuable, and Python is a plus. Strong Linux and cloud fundamentals, ideally GCP and Kubernetes.
  • Deep experience with secure architecture and authentication and authorization patterns, and with building security building blocks that other teams adopt.
  • Hands-on experience securing AI-powered systems or agent features, and a clear point of view on how AI changes application security.
  • The judgment to make hard risk calls under ambiguity, and the influence to align technical and non-technical leaders without formal authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading security for AI-native products, internal agents, or AI-assisted engineering workflows at scale.
  • Experience building or scaling a security champions or developer enablement program.
  • Public security work, such as CVEs, research, talks, or open-source tools, or certifications such as OSCP or OSWE.

Example Success Outcomes

  • An AppSec strategy tied to Security department KRs, with supporting work committed in other teams’ roadmaps.
  • A measurable drop in high-risk vulnerability classes, backed by shared guardrails or libraries.
  • AI-assisted AppSec workflows adopted by teams outside Security, with clear gains in speed or signal quality.

Our Tech Stack

React on the front end; Ruby, Ruby on Rails, Python, MongoDB, and Elasticsearch on the backend; Kubernetes, Docker, and Terraform in infrastructure; GCP for cloud.

This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Apollo and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

This is not a research seat where models get handed off to someone else's pipeline — you design the strategy, write the code, deploy it, and own it in production. If you want your models allocating real capital onchain within weeks of joining, read on.

Depending on your background and interests, you'll join one of our vault strategy teams. Our strategies span lending and credit curation, cross-chain yield aggregation, structured products, RWAs, and more. Teams own the full strategy lifecycle: research and protocol due diligence, strategy design and backtesting, allocation and rebalancing engines, onchain execution and optimization, and 24/7 monitoring of live positions. You own strategies end-to-end and are accountable for their performance, safety, and uptime.

What you'll do;

  • Design and ship vault strategies: take a strategy from thesis and design doc through implementation, simulation, deployment, and live operation — RWAs, leveraged lending, yield aggregation, cross-protocol allocation, perpetuals, prediction markets, and new product types we haven't built yet.
  • Optimize strategies: signals research, execution optimization, gas-aware rebalancing across tokens and chains, liquidity and duration management.
  • Run protocol and asset due diligence: evaluate new protocols, collateral assets, and chains for inclusion in strategies — solvency mechanics, oracle design, redemption paths, liquidity depth, and more.
  • Own risk parameters: supply caps, LLTV settings, concentration limits, VaR-based exposure models, and automated de-risking logic that pulls positions when conditions deteriorate.
  • Integrate new protocols and chains: build and validate adapters for lending markets, DEX aggregators, and bridges; verify strategy behavior against forked-chain simulation before capital touches it.
  • Monitor what you build: extend our risk-monitoring and alerting systems, define the conditions that page someone, and participate in the on-call rotation for the strategies you own.
  • Support launches and clients: partner with growth, capital markets, and client teams on new vault and strategy launches.

Requirements

  • A track record of building quantitative systems that run in production — algorithmic trading, portfolio optimization, market making, or risk systems at a trading firm, asset manager, fintech, or crypto-native company. This is often 2–8 years of experience, but we weight what you've built over years on a résumé.
  • You write the code behind your strategies. Strong Python and solid software-engineering fundamentals: testing, code review, and the judgment to build durable abstractions rather than one-off scripts. This is a hands-on, quantitative role — not a discretionary trading seat.
  • Applied quantitative skills: optimization, statistics, and simulation, and the instinct to validate models against real data before trusting them.
  • Comfort with data infrastructure: SQL and experience building or consuming data pipelines.
  • Production ownership: you've debugged live systems under pressure and understand that a strategy managing other people's money has to be correct, monitored, and recoverable.

- Clear technical communication.

Bonus points

  • Hands-on DeFi experience: lending protocols, ERC-4626 vaults, AMMs, or oracle systems — as a builder or a sophisticated user.
  • Solidity / EVM literacy: reading protocol contracts, forked-chain simulation (anvil), or writing adapters; non-EVM experience (e.g., Solana) also valued.
  • On-chain operational experience: multisig workflows, transaction submission and signing infrastructure, bridging.
  • TypeScript, and familiarity with a modern data stack (e.g., BigQuery, Dagster, Hex, GCP/Kubernetes).
  • Experience with risk modeling for volatile or thinly-traded assets: VaR, liquidation modeling, stress testing.

Who thrives here;

  • Wants end-to-end ownership — research, code, deployment, and the pager — not a hand-off between research and engineering.
  • Comfortable that crypto markets don't close. Strategy owners take on-call seriously, and the occasional market-event night is part of the job; we staff and rotate to keep it sustainable.
  • Operates well in ambiguity: can take "we should have a strategy for X" and return a scoped design, not a list of questions — and is comfortable in a fast-moving space where priorities and team structure evolve.
  • Holds a genuine risk view and voices it — including "we shouldn't do this" when the analysis says so.
  • Pragmatic about shipping: balances rigor against client timelines without cutting corners on safety.
  • Naturally curious about digital assets and DeFi. Deep crypto experience is not required — curiosity and strong quant fundamentals are.

Benefits

  • Regular in-person company retreats and cross-country "office visit" perk

- $1,000 WFH stipend

  • Monthly reimbursement for home internet, phone, and cellular data

- Unlimited vacation

- 100% paid parental leave of 12 weeks

- Fertility benefits

- Opportunity for incentive compensation

Please note at this time our hiring is reserved for potential employees who are able to work within the contiguous United States and Canada. Should you need alternative accommodations, please note that in your application.

jobs.description:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

About Apollo

Apollo is the AI-powered go-to-market platform that helps revenue teams find, engage, and convert their best customers. We combine a database of more than 210 million contacts and 35 million companies with an agentic end-to-end GTM platform, and more than 500,000 companies rely on us to run their go-to-market motion. We are profitable, growing fast, and rebuilding the product around AI and agents.

About Builder Studio

Builder Studio is Apollo's new product for building custom GTM software in plain English. A RevOps lead, GTM engineer, or founder describes the tool they need, and Builder Studio plans it, generates real code, and turns it into a working app they can preview, refine through conversation, publish, and share with their team.

Every app is made of four building blocks: Pages for the interface, Databases for structured records, Workflows for visible backend logic and scheduled jobs, and Agents that reason over Apollo context and take action. What makes it different from a generic app builder is that Apollo's data, enrichment, sequences, deliverability, and CRM sync are native building blocks, not bolted-on third-party integrations.

It is one of Apollo's flagship AI bets. The product is in the hands of early design partners now and is heading toward broad launch, which means the next year is about taking a working product and making it reliable, secure, and loved at scale.

Your role and mission

You will own major slices of Builder Studio end to end, across the builder experience customers see and the systems that make generated apps actually run. You will work on problems most engineers have never touched: an agent that writes and edits software on a customer's behalf, a runtime that safely executes that code with the user's own Apollo permissions, and an interface that makes all of it understandable to someone who has never read a line of code.

What you will do

  • Build the core Studio experience: the chat-driven build loop, live preview, canvas, and the publish and share flow, so a non-technical user can go from an idea to a working tool in minutes
  • Shape how the agent turns a natural-language goal into a plan, a set of pages, databases, and workflows, and then safely applies follow-up edits without breaking what already works
  • Design the runtime and workflow layer for generated apps, including triggers, scheduled jobs, retries, logging, and the line between deterministic steps and agentic steps
  • Own delegated identity, permissions, secrets, and isolation so generated apps act with exactly the access the user has, and nothing more
  • Expand "connect once, use anywhere" integrations across Apollo data (contacts, companies, lists) and external systems like Google Sheets, Google Drive, CRMs, and MCP-based connectors
  • Make the relationships between pages, data, workflows, and agents legible in the UI, so customers trust what their app is doing
  • Work directly with design partners and customers, turn their feedback into shipped improvements quickly, and help define what the product becomes
  • Raise the quality bar on a fast-moving 0 to 1 team: set patterns, write the tests and evals that matter, and own reliability, performance, and cost of what you ship

How we work: AI-native by default

You treat AI-assisted development as a core part of how you work. You use agents to move faster on design, investigation, and implementation, with clear judgment about where to review closely, and you look for ways AI raises the leverage of the whole team. On Builder Studio this is doubly true: you are building an AI that writes software, so your own instincts for where AI-generated code succeeds and fails directly shape the product.

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years building and shipping production software, with real depth on both the frontend and backend of the same product
  • Strong TypeScript and React skills, including complex, stateful UIs such as editors, canvases, builders, or real-time collaborative surfaces
  • Solid backend and API design experience, ideally including event-driven or workflow systems where retries, idempotency, and observability matter
  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs in production: agent loops, tool calling, context management, code generation, or evals. You know where models break and how to design around it
  • Comfort making sound security calls on systems that run untrusted or generated code: sandboxing, delegated auth, scoped tokens, and secrets handling
  • A track record of taking an ambiguous 0 to 1 product from rough prototype to something customers rely on, and making the scope-versus-quality calls that requires
  • Product instinct and empathy for non-technical users. You care whether a RevOps lead can understand what their app is doing, not just whether the code is correct
  • Genuine, current fluency with AI-assisted development and a high bar for quality and ownership

Nice to have

  • Experience building low-code, no-code, or AI app-builder products, or developer tools
  • Experience with edge or serverless runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects
  • Experience with Ruby on Rails at scale
  • Background in GTM, sales, or marketing tech, or experience working closely with RevOps teams

Our tech stack

TypeScript and React on the front end; Ruby on Rails and Node.js on the backend; Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects for the Builder Studio runtime; Python, MongoDB, and Elasticsearch across the wider platform; Kubernetes, Docker, and Terraform in infrastructure; GCP for cloud.

What you will love about Apollo

You will help build a brand new product from the ground up at a company with the data, distribution, and customer base to make it matter on day one. You will work with a small, high-bar team, own real scope, and have the AI tooling and budget to work at the top of your leverage.

Compensation and benefits

The listed Pay Range reflects the annual base salary for this role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Apollo and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate's experience, qualifications, and location.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity; company bonus; paid holidays, flex PTO, and parental leave; employee assistance program and wellbeing benefits; global travel coverage; life and disability insurance; and extended health, dental, and vision benefits.

We are AI Native

Apollo.io is an AI-native company built on a culture of continuous improvement. We're on the front lines of driving productivity for our customers, and we expect the same mindset from our team. If you're energized by finding smarter, faster ways to get things done using AI and automation, you'll thrive here.

Why You'll Love Working at Apollo

jobs.excerpt: About CircleCI EngineeringCI/CD has been solved.  Now it's being reinvented.
jobs.description:
About CircleCI Engineering

CI/CD has been solved. Now it's being reinvented. AI agents don't just run pipelines. They write code, trigger builds, interpret failures, and propose fixes. The interfaces that developers use to understand and trust that work don't exist yet. We're building them.

At CircleCI, our guiding principles aren't posters on a wall. We learn fast: we run experiments, accept failure, and scale what works. We think like the customer: every decision connects back to the developer sitting in front of a failing build at 2 am. We own the outcome: not just our slice of it, but the whole thing. If that's how you already work, you'll fit here.

About the Query Team

Every pipeline, job, and test that runs on CircleCI generates data, and that history is one of our biggest advantages in an agentic software delivery lifecycle. Flaky test detection, test insights, pipeline search, and agents that reason about why a build failed all depend on fast, reliable access to it.

The Query team owns the system that makes this possible. We pull product data out of the transactional services that create it and store it in datastores built for historical and analytical workloads. We serve it through domain-level APIs to CircleCI's product teams and to customers through our public API. Our goal is to make storing data "fire and forget" for every other team, and querying it fast and dependable at a scale that keeps growing.

What You'll Do

  • Build AI-natively. AI is how we work. It's not a productivity layer on top of engineering, but the default starting point for how problems get approached and solved.
  • Shape how we store data at scale. Own and harden our ClickHouse-based storage layer. Design schemas for known and emerging access patterns, and tune ingestion and query performance to support production-scale data.
  • Build the pipelines that move our data. Design and own ingestion from event streams and durable workflows built on Temporal. Data should arrive reliably, stay queryable while it's in transit, and never slow down the critical path of the services that produce it.
  • Serve data to the product and to customers. Evolve our platform into the default path for historical queries. Make getting historical data easy, not a bottleneck. Teams should be able to get what they need quickly and with minimal hand-holding, while Query keeps enough visibility into how the data is used to optimize ingestion and reads across every consumer. Build in the indexing, caching, and tiered storage required to keep it performant.
  • Set technical direction. When the problem is complex or the answer isn't obvious, you lead the design discussion, write up the architecture decision, and make the call. You help decide which data domain we migrate next and how.
  • Champion observability. Use Honeycomb, Datadog, and Rollbar to understand ingestion lag, query latency, and data correctness. For a data platform, operational data drives stability, not just incident response.
  • Keep things moving. You take ambiguous data problems from design to production quickly, and you help the people around you move faster too.

You don't just patch problems, you ask why they happened. You'll fix the immediate issue, then solve the underlying team practice, process, or system that let it through.

What You'll Bring

  • AI-native engineering practices. You use AI tools daily and can speak to what you've built, where they changed your approach, and where they fall short.
  • Hands-on data experience. You've built or owned data-intensive systems such as ingestion pipelines, event-driven architectures, or analytical and time-series datastores. You understand the tradeoffs between transactional and analytical storage, and you've designed schemas and tuned queries for high-volume workloads. Experience with ClickHouse or another columnar database is a strong plus.
  • Backend depth in Go. You're strong in Go, or strong in a comparable language and eager to work in Go: interface design, data modeling, service integration, and concurrency. Familiarity with React and TypeScript is a plus, since you'll occasionally work on the product surfaces that display this data.
  • Distributed systems judgment. You understand delivery guarantees, idempotency, backpressure, and failure recovery. You know when to rely on a framework's reliability guarantees rather than building your own.
  • Technical leadership. You've led the design of complex systems and made tradeoffs deliberately. You leave foundations others can build on. You raise the quality bar through reviews, mentoring, and direct feedback, not just through the code you write.
  • A track record of shipping. 5+ years building and operating production backend systems. Your work has served real users, and you've treated latency, reliability, and correctness as design concerns.

Sound like you?

You care about how data powers the product, not just where it lives. You know how to make a datastore fast at scale, and have tuned schemas and queries against real production load. You think like a platform engineer, measuring your work by how much it unblocks the teams building on it. AI isn't a tool you reach for occasionally; it's a core part of how you approach and solve problems. If that sounds like you, we want to talk.

How CircleCI Uses AI in Hiring

About Sayari:

Sayari is the judgment infrastructure for trustworthy AI in economic security and commercial risk. The Sayari Commercial World Model resolves 11.7B+ primary-source records from 250+ jurisdictions forming the ground truth of global commerce. A Judgment Ontology, encoding over a decade of investigative tradecraft, and Superconductor, an agentic orchestration platform, deliver AI that reasons like an expert analyst, shows its work, and traces every finding to its source. Trusted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, HM Revenue & Customs, and Fortune 500 enterprises, Sayari is used by thousands of professionals across 35+ countries to secure supply chains and dismantle illicit networks. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., with offices in London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Tel Aviv.

About the Role

Sayari’s customers buy answers to hard problems: who really owns a supplier, where a sanctioned network is moving goods, which alerts deserve an analyst’s time. Sayari’s AI platform Superconductor delivers those answers at machine scale. It is built in the field, with analysts and engineers working alongside customers to define what it needs to do.

The Field Intelligence Analyst brings Sayari’s tradecraft to that work. You scope the problem, design the solution, prove its value, and deliver mission impact. You own the analytical relationship for a portfolio of accounts, from first conversation through sustained delivery. What you learn on live engagements flows back into Superconductor and into Sayari’s tradecraft standard.

You work in our Field Intelligence Department, a global team of analysts deployed to support government agencies and Fortune 500 companies. You sit in the same org as Forward Deployed Engineers and the Product team. The field shapes the roadmap, and Product sets it.

Why This Role Exists

  • Customers buy answers. Superconductor reasons like an expert analyst at machine scale. The analyst’s job shifts from producing every answer by hand to directing, validating, and extending what Superconductor produces, and teaching customer analysts to do the same.
  • Context should survive the contract. The analyst who designed the proof-of-value knows why the success criteria are what they are. Keeping that analyst on the account protects delivery quality and surfaces the next problem before the customer names it.
  • Tradecraft is built in the field. Field Intelligence Analysts see what was promised, what was delivered, and what the customer did with it. That full view produces better methodology, better evals, and a better Superconductor than any single-phase role can.

What You Will Do

Own the analytical relationship, end to end

  • Run discovery and proof-of-value engagements anchored on work the customer already pays people to do, such as alert adjudication, due diligence, investigations, and case prioritization. Define success criteria you will personally be accountable for delivering.
  • Stay on the account after close and deliver the work you scoped. This includes multi-hop investigations across ownership, trade, and corporate records, plus analytical briefings and training.
  • Serve as the customer’s single analytical point of contact from first conversation through renewal.

Build with Field Engineering and Product

  • Pair with FDEs on discovery and delivery. You define the analytical requirement, they build it, and you validate it against the mission.
  • When something built for one customer should be rebuilt for many, make the case to Product with evidence: the problem, the workaround, and the customers who share it.
  • Document where the platform falls short of the mission, with raw examples attached.

Deliver analyst-plus-AI, and teach it

  • Direct Superconductor against live mission problems. Validate its reasoning against expert standards, and extend it into new customer workflows.
  • Train and certify customer analysts on Sayari methods and on working with Superconductor. Identify the customer experts who should go further.

Build the tradecraft

  • Capture the judgment calls, non-obvious pivots, and creative approaches from live engagements. Contribute them to the Tradecraft team as expert-annotated reference cases, eval scenarios, and training material.
  • Hold your work to the Field Intelligence standard, and help raise it.

Support Go-To-Market Teams

  • Work with Sales to diagnose customer problems, scope solutions, and deliver mission impact.

Who You Are

Required

  • A builder’s temperament and comfort with ambiguity. You do well on small teams with end-to-end ownership and no defined lane, working next to engineers on things that don’t exist yet.
  • Experience conducting complex, multi-source investigations in one or more of these areas: financial crime, sanctions and export controls, supply chain and forced labor risk, transnational criminal organizations, or law enforcement and intelligence investigations. This should include work with corporate records, trade data, and OSINT.
  • Customer-facing range. You have scoped engagements, demonstrated capability to skeptical experts, and delivered under a statement of work. Candidates often come from solutions consulting, services delivery, embedded analytics, or mission-support roles.
  • Hands-on fluency directing and evaluating AI and agentic analytical tools. You can define what “right” looks like precisely enough to test against.

Desired
